verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on Friday, April 10, 2026, at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'scheduled to splash down at around 8:07 p.m. EDT on Friday, April 10 ... off the San Diego coast ... Splashing down locally at 5:07 pm PDT'; R2: 'Splashdown is targeted for 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'around 8:07 p.m. ET in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California'
verifications.reasoning: All references directly confirm the exact location, date, and times for the Artemis II splashdown.

verifications.claim: The splashdown marks the end of the crewed lunar flyby mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'return to Earth today (April 10) to end a 10-day test flight around the moon'; R2: 'completing the Artemis II crew’s return to Earth'; R3: 'the historic mission ... comes to an end'; R5: 'NASA’s Artemis II mission will come to an end on Friday, April 10'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state the splashdown ends the crewed lunar flyby mission.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The crew will be met by team members from NASA and the U.S. Navy'; R2: 'a combined NASA and U.S. military recovery team will be standing by'; R3: 'recovery teams will airlift the astronauts'; R6: 'Recovery teams will retrieve the crew'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm recovery teams are prepared and standing by for the crew.

verifications.claim: Live coverage is on NASA+ and major streaming platforms starting around 6:30 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Live coverage begins at 6:30 pm EDT ... NASA+ streaming service ... Netflix, Amazon Prime'; R2: 'Watch live return coverage on NASA+ ... starting at 6:30 p.m.'; R3: 'NASA's coverage ... begin at 6:30 p.m. ET on ... NASA+ ... Amazon Prime ... Netflix'
verifications.reasoning: Exact times and platforms including NASA+ and major streamers are specified across sources.

verifications.claim: The crew module separates from the service module at 7:33 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '7:33 p.m. EDT (2333 GMT): Crew Module and Service Module separate'; R2: '7:33 p.m.: Orion’s crew module will separate from the service module'
verifications.reasoning: Precise time for crew/service module separation directly stated.

verifications.claim: The capsule enters Earth's atmosphere at 7:53 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '7:53 p.m. EDT (2353 GMT): Entry Interface occurs and the Orion capsule re-enters Earth's atmosphere'; R2: '7:53 p.m.: ... first contact with the upper atmosphere'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time for atmospheric entry (entry interface) confirmed.

verifications.claim: The capsule's atmospheric entry causes a brief communication blackout.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'planned six-minute communications blackout as plasma builds around the capsule'; R5: '16-minute re-entry blackout'; R6: 'Communication blackout (23:53-23:59 GMT) ... plasma layer around the capsule'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly describe atmospheric entry causing a communications blackout due to plasma.

verifications.claim: The mission marks the first crewed lunar mission in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first crewed lunar mission in more than 53 years'; R2: 'first humans toward the Moon since 1972 ... more than 50 years'; R3: 'first humans to fly on a moon mission in over 50 years'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state it is the first crewed lunar mission since Apollo in over 50 years.

verifications.claim: The crew is testing systems for future lunar landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'testing life-support systems, navigation, communications ... support future lunar landing missions'; R3: 'testing systems and hardware ahead of a future moon landing'; R4: 'testing systems and hardware ahead of a future moon landing'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm crew testing systems to support future lunar landings.
